page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual machine in the High Frequency Compute family, provisioned on an x86_64 Intel platform. It provides 4 shared virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard vector extensions such as AVX, FMA, and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and comes bundled with 384 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. It lacks dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1625.0 and a multi-core score of 4781.0, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 7697.28 and stress-ng results of 2411.16 single-core and 8740.87 multi-core. Software compilation via Clang reached 7042.0 points, while small-block cached memory bandwidth proved strong at 497.33 GB/sec. However, uncached 256 MB memory read and write bandwidths tested lower at 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively. Disk and algorithmic throughput also presented weaker throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and static web serving.

The shared CPU allocation and modest clock speed represent key operational tradeoffs, causing performance variance under sustained peak CPU or memory bandwidth stress. In terms of cost efficiency, the integration of 384 GB of fast NVMe storage alongside balanced compute and memory capacity offers reliable utility without needing external block storage attachments. This profile makes the instance effective for general-purpose application hosting, staging environments, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD build workers, and small-to-medium web backend services.
description: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a High Frequency Compute instance delivering 4 shared vCPUs on an Intel x86_64 platform with 2 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a 2.0 GHz clock rate. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 384 GB of onboard NVMe SSD storage and a public IPv4 address without bundled GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show balanced mid-tier outcomes across Geekbench, stress-ng, and Clang compilation tasks, while handling up to 6.0 million Redis SET operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput show lower relative efficiency due to shared resource allocation. This server offers cost-effective utility for self-contained workloads needing fast local storage, such as web application hosting, caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and microservice deployments.
